input.bug_report: Creators are able to submit duplicate applications to the same campaign. A creator who already has a submitted application to campaign 'camp-abc' can POST another application and it succeeds with 201 instead of receiving a 409 Conflict. The duplicate-check query in the repository seems to be looking for the wrong records — it only finds withdrawn applications instead of active ones, so the active application is never detected and the duplicate check always passes.

from sqlalchemy import func, select

            Application.id == application_id, Application.is_deleted.is_(False)

            Application.campaign_id == campaign_id,

gold_standard.root_cause: Wrong comparison operator in get_active_by_creator_and_campaign. The query uses `Application.status == ApplicationStatus.WITHDRAWN` (equals) instead of `Application.status != ApplicationStatus.WITHDRAWN` (not equals). This means the method only finds withdrawn applications instead of active ones. Since there are no withdrawn applications, it always returns None, and the duplicate check in submit_application always passes.
gold_standard.fix_diff:
--- a/app/repositories/application_repo.py
+++ b/app/repositories/application_repo.py
@@ -21,7 +21,7 @@
         query = select(Application).where(
             Application.creator_id == creator_id,
             Application.campaign_id == campaign_id,
-            Application.status == ApplicationStatus.WITHDRAWN,
+            Application.status != ApplicationStatus.WITHDRAWN,
             Application.is_deleted.is_(False),
         )
         result = await self.db.execute(query)
gold_standard.fix_explanation: Change `==` to `!=` in the status filter of get_active_by_creator_and_campaign. The method should find active (non-withdrawn) applications to prevent duplicates. With `==`, it only looks for withdrawn applications, so active duplicates are never detected.
